name: connect-model-profisee-to-profisee-target-build
description: What: Build the Connect model on the Profisee to Profisee target instance from the spec (empty-model bootstrap): delete this family if present (PDataProfiseeToProfiseeImport, the retired name PDataProfiseeToProfiseeExport, then the 50 Dba domains), create the domains with the same ids as Main and load their rows (unless kept), create PDataProfiseeToProfiseeImport, verify. Never deletes another entity (also not the Main-role entities on a shared server); keeps the domains when another entity on the target uses them (the CRUD base on the same instance) and all 50 have their spec ids, otherwise stops first. Why: A building block of the Connect pack; a test, setup or schedule workload runs it so its steps exist once. When: Never run directly once the pack is tested; its parents run it. Running it alone is safe only when its own Needs are met. Needs: reference values: connect/instances:ProfiseeToProfiseeInstanceName, connect/machines:ProfiseeToProfiseeServerNameFQDN. Success: Every step Succeeded or Skipped. If it fails: Run connect-preflight first; then open the first failed step, whose If it fails text names what to check.
globalParametersNotes: Spec: C:\devops\repos\speed-merchants\CrewChief\connect-model-spec. The domains carry the same ids as on Main, so the export entity's domain attributes bind on either side. DomainsToCreate is set during the run by Decide Domain Create (true or false); it starts blank so no domain step runs before that decision.

inline.description: What: Gateway check: list entities. Accepts ONLY 200 so a wrong address (404) or a wrong key (401) stops the run before anything is created or deleted. Why: Calls the Profisee or TestAuto REST API for this change or check, the same way a client would. Success: The response status is one of the expected codes (200). If it fails: 401 = the API key is not set on that instance yet (run connect-setup) or the secret is wrong; 404 = the record, entity or address is missing; no response = the server in the URL (connect/urls, connect/machines) is down.

What: Fail fast when the instance's Maestro model id differs from the spec (spec.json modelId), before anything is deleted or created. Why: Does work no single built-in step does (several calls, waits or checks in one place) and stops at the first problem. Success: The script finishes without an error; its output lines say what it did. If it fails: Read the last output line and the error text: the script names the value, server or record it could not handle.

What: Delete this family if present (absent is fine): 2 entities, then the 50 Dba domains. Warns about other entities and leaves them alone. When one of them uses a Dba domain (the CRUD base on the same instance does) the domains are kept and only this family's entities are deleted, provided all 50 exist with their spec ids; otherwise it stops before deleting anything and names the domains that differ. Why: Does work no single built-in step does (several calls, waits or checks in one place) and stops at the first problem. Success: The script finishes without an error; its output lines say what it did. If it fails: Read the last output line and the error text: the script names the value, server or record it could not handle.

What: Look at the 50 Dba domains on the target and print true when none exists (the steps below create and load them) or false when all 50 exist with their spec ids (kept: another entity uses them), into the run value DomainsToCreate. Why: the target can be an instance whose own model already holds the domains (the CRUD base); they are never written over. Success: true or false is printed. If it fails: some domains exist and others do not, or an id differs from the spec; the message names them. Empty the model first.
